title: Devcontainer: coding agents, hooks, and the git wrapper
summary: This change turns the devcontainer from a Rust-only image into a full agent workspace. The Dockerfile now pins and installs moon, Node 22, pnpm, Bun, gh, actionlint, uv, the NVIDIA skill linters, and four coding agents (codex, claude-code, opencode, omp), builds the repo's own dsh/omp/opencode integrations from the pnpm lockfile, and wires each agent's hook config to `osf hook` at a root-owned, read-only path. The git wrapper is rewritten to force the hooks path per-invocation under a configurable workspace root instead of a system-wide core.hooksPath, and a battery of build-time tests proves the wrapper, the hooks, the skills, and each agent binary actually work for the dev user.

lanes.label: Image build
lanes.subtitle: Dockerfile layers
lanes.summary: The Dockerfile grows from a Rust toolchain plus git-town into a multi-toolchain image: pinned downloads verified by SHA-256, the repo's own integrations built from the pnpm lockfile, and build-time test scripts that fail the build.

lanes.label: Coding agents
lanes.subtitle: dev user, /workspace
lanes.summary: Four coding agents installed as global npm packages, each usable as builder or reviewer, each with its own hook mechanism pointed at osf hook.

lanes.label: osf tooling
lanes.subtitle: /opt/factory/bin
lanes.summary: The osf binary, the git wrapper, and the root-owned git hooks. The wrapper now forces the hooks path per call rather than relying on system git config.

lanes.label: Repository workspace
lanes.subtitle: bind-mounted at /workspace
lanes.summary: The checked-out repository the dev user edits, including .claude/hooks.json and the integrations whose dist output the image copies out.

nodes.label: Dockerfile
nodes.subtitle: pinned toolchain installs
nodes.summary: Adds pinned, checksum-verified installs for moon, gh, actionlint, uv, Node 22, pnpm via corepack, Bun, and the four coding agents; installs SkillSpector and SkillEvaluator through uv; builds the dsh/omp/opencode integrations from the pnpm lockfile; and runs six build-time test scripts before the image is considered good.

nodes.label: agents.json
nodes.subtitle: one list of agents and hooks
nodes.summary: The single source of truth for which coding agents the image installs, their roles, their hook events, their hook paths, and where an agent's own hook system falls short of osf hook's two events. The hook test reads this file instead of naming agents in its own code.

nodes.label: devcontainer.json
nodes.subtitle: workspace mount and postCreate
nodes.summary: Pins the workspace bind mount to /workspace, forwards GH_TOKEN from the host, and extends postCreateCommand to check moon, node and pnpm alongside osf.

nodes.label: devcontainer-image workflow
nodes.subtitle: CI build of the image
nodes.summary: A GitHub Actions workflow that builds the devcontainer image, so the Dockerfile's own build-time tests run in CI as well as locally.

nodes.label: Build-time tests
nodes.subtitle: six scripts run during docker build
nodes.summary: git-wrapper.sh, git-hooks.sh, agent-hooks.sh, skills-installed.sh, dsh-starts.sh, coding-agent-tools.sh and builder-tools.sh each run inside the build and fail it on a broken wrapper, hook, skill install, or agent binary.

nodes.label: dsh package-lock.json
nodes.subtitle: @deepseek-ai/dsh 0.2.0-rc.2
nodes.summary: A dedicated npm lockfile for dsh, installed with npm ci into /opt/dsh so the agent's dependency tree is reproducible and separate from the repo's pnpm workspace.

nodes.label: dsh
nodes.subtitle: default builder
nodes.summary: Installed from its own lockfile and symlinked onto PATH. Its factory profile registers the repo's writing-check plugin for stop and the Claude-format hooks bridge for prompt; the profile directory is root-owned and read-only while the rest of ~/.dsh stays writable.

nodes.label: Claude Code
nodes.subtitle: managed settings
nodes.summary: Installed globally and wired through /etc/claude-code/managed-settings.json, a root-owned read-only file that calls osf hook for both stop and prompt.

nodes.label: Codex
nodes.subtitle: managed hooks dir
nodes.summary: Installed globally and wired through /etc/codex, with a requirements file forcing the managed hooks directory. Codex has no turn-end event, so only user_prompt_submit is wired.

nodes.label: opencode
nodes.subtitle: system config plugin
nodes.summary: Installed globally and wired through /etc/opencode/opencode.json, which names the repo's own opencode plugin built from integrations/opencode and copied to /opt/factory/opencode-plugin.

nodes.label: omp
nodes.subtitle: global extension
nodes.summary: Installed globally and wired through a root-owned, read-only hook directory under dev's home, since omp has no system-level hooks location. Runs on Bun rather than plain Node.

nodes.label: osf
nodes.subtitle: /opt/factory/bin/osf
nodes.summary: Built from the workspace and installed read-only. Its config and repository modules gained the workspace-root and hook-related settings the wrapper and agents read.

nodes.label: git wrapper
nodes.subtitle: /opt/factory/bin/git
nodes.summary: Refuses --no-verify and -n on commit and --no-verify on push, then forces core.hooksPath on the command line for every git call under OSF_WORKSPACE_ROOT. It no longer relies on a system-wide core.hooksPath, so scratch repositories under /tmp are unaffected.

nodes.label: git hooks
nodes.subtitle: pre-commit, commit-msg, pre-push
nodes.summary: Root-owned, read-only hook scripts that each call osf. The wrapper points git at this directory explicitly for repositories under the workspace.

nodes.label: osf-path.sh
nodes.subtitle: login shell PATH
nodes.summary: A profile.d script that restores osf, the cargo toolchain, and the agent binaries to PATH after a login shell resets it.

nodes.label: Repository checkout
nodes.subtitle: bind-mounted at /workspace
nodes.summary: The working tree the dev user edits. The image builds the integrations from this tree's lockfile and copies their dist output into root-owned locations.

nodes.label: .claude/hooks.json
nodes.subtitle: dsh prompt bridge target
nodes.summary: A tracked, dev-editable file that dsh's Claude-format prompt bridge reads, because that bridge resolves its config path relative to the launch directory rather than the profile directory.

nodes.label: integrations/dsh
nodes.subtitle: writing-check plugin
nodes.summary: The repo's own dsh plugin, built from the pnpm lockfile and copied into the factory profile's node_modules. Its index gained the hook wiring the profile registers.

nodes.label: docs/development.md
nodes.subtitle: how the container works
nodes.summary: Documents the wrapper's forced hooks path, the agent list, the default builder, and how to run each check by hand.

edges.label: npm install -g
edges.summary: The Dockerfile installs each coding agent as a global npm package pinned to an exact version.

edges.label: hook wiring follows this list
edges.summary: The Dockerfile's hook installs and the agent-hooks test both follow the one list in agents.json.

edges.label: sh <test>.sh
edges.summary: Each test script runs during the build and fails it on a broken wrapper, hook, skill install, or agent binary.

edges.label: pnpm --filter build
edges.summary: The image builds the repo's own dsh, omp and opencode integrations from the workspace lockfile, then copies their dist output into root-owned locations.

edges.label: -c core.hooksPath=/opt/factory/githooks
edges.summary: The wrapper now forces the hooks path on the command line for every git call under the workspace root, replacing the system-wide core.hooksPath the image used to set.

edges.label: osf hook stop / prompt
edges.summary: dsh's factory profile registers the repo's writing-check plugin for stop and the Claude-format bridge for prompt, both of which invoke osf hook.

edges.label: prompt bridge configPath
edges.summary: The prompt bridge resolves its config path relative to the launch directory, so it points at the tracked .claude/hooks.json rather than a root-owned home-relative file.

flows.title: A coding agent's stop hook runs osf
flows.summary: When a coding agent finishes a turn, its own hook mechanism invokes osf hook, which runs the writing check and returns a verdict the agent acts on.

messages.label: turn ends
messages.note: dsh's stop plugin reads the reply from the session directly, so it needs no config file.

flows.title: A commit under the workspace runs the forced hooks
flows.summary: The wrapper forces the hooks path on the command line, so a commit under the workspace runs the root-owned hooks even though no system-wide core.hooksPath is set.

messages.label: -c core.hooksPath=...
messages.note: Forced per invocation, so a scratch repository under /tmp keeps its own hooks.

views.title: Container architecture
views.summary: The image build produces the agent runtime, the osf tooling, and the workspace mount; the agents and the git wrapper both reach osf.

views.title: Hook wiring per agent
views.summary: Each agent's own hook mechanism and the path it is wired through, all converging on osf hook.

views.title: Image build pipeline
views.summary: What the Dockerfile installs, builds, and proves before the image is considered good.
